purpose: Every place where the product and G1.11's claims and provenance rules disagree today. scripts/claims-gate.ts (pnpm gate:claims) runs ten checks: the citation register's schema, the local snapshot of every non-permanent source, the claim register's evidence, the surfaces claims name, every provenance expression built in src/, the provenance attribute on every claim or figure element, the exempt-numeral rule, report-body registration, template citation registration, and the seven designated surfaces. Each check compares what it finds against the matching group here in both directions: an unlisted divergence fails, and a listed one that no longer exists fails too, so a fix has to bring the ledger down with it and nothing can quietly give a registration back.
notAnApproval: Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. Every entry below is an open finding measured exactly, not an accepted state — acceptance is a line in docs/acceptance-matrix.md, and G1.11 stands at NO there. The point of the ledger is that the distance from the rule is written down and can only shrink.
howEntriesAreMatched: The seven checks whose findings name a single record hold the finding sentence verbatim, because there is nothing in it to recount. The three that carry counts — report-body registration, template citation registration and the designated surfaces — hold the counts, and scripts/claims-gate.ts rebuilds the sentence from them through the same function the check itself uses. So one prose block gaining a registration moves a number, and a number that moves fails in both directions rather than matching a stale sentence.
granularity: The report-body backlog is 675 unregistered prose blocks. It is recorded as 16 entries, one per template file, each carrying its own counts, and that is deliberate: 675 rows would be 675 copies of one sentence and would hide the shape of the work rather than show it. docs/figures-register.json takes the same decision where it records one shape-level invariant instead of 298 identical figure rows. The per-file counts are still exact, and the check still reads every one of the 746 blocks: nothing is rounded, only grouped.
citationSchemaNote: Empty, and checked in both directions so it cannot stay empty through a regression. All 19 entries in data/citations.json carry the eight fields G1.11 names, a type inside pmid|doi|statute|registry|regulator|dataset, a resolvable https URL, a real calendar access date and a supporting quotation of 25 words or fewer.
sourceSnapshotNote: Empty for the same reason. Seven of the 19 sources are Ensembl records, which are live web pages rather than permanent identifiers, and all seven carry a local snapshot under docs/sources/ensembl/ that exists on disk. The other twelve are PMIDs and one DOI, which C4 exempts because they resolve to a fixed record.
claimEvidenceNote: Empty: every one of the 71 canonical claims carries verbatim text, at least one surface, and at least one piece of evidence whose citation is in data/citations.json with an accessed_on equal to that source's access_date. This is the half of G1.11 that is finished, over the eight reports it covers.
claimSurfaceNote: Empty: every surface the 71 claims name resolves — a page route in docs/route-register.json, the export:account-export-v1 contract, or the research-digest mail fixture — and every report slug named is one a template in data/templates publishes.

figureProvenance.finding: src/components/embryo/compare/compare-cell.tsx builds a citation provenance whose id is the expression withinFamily.citation_ids[0], which no static reader can resolve
figureProvenance.why: The four other findings in this group were defects and are fixed: three named modules nobody had written, and one could emit `citation:` with an empty id through a `?? ""`. This one is not a defect and cannot be made into a literal. A within-family figure's citation is the publication the stored numbers were measured under, and it arrives on the `embryo_scores.finding` row with them; which citation it is depends on the row, so the id is a runtime value by construction. The closed eight-key finding carries no score-row id either, so there is no `seed:` target to name in its place. The correctness the check was protecting is now enforced by types rather than by the string: `citedWithinFamily` in src/lib/embryos/policy.ts is the only way to those numbers and returns the row only when it carries both its numbers and its citation, so a figure that claims a citation cannot render without one.
figureProvenance.closing: Nothing to close in src/. Closing it in the gate means teaching the reader to resolve a citation id that comes from a named database column - checking that the column exists and that every id any row of it holds is in data/citations.json, which is a database-backed check rather than a static one and belongs with the rendered-DOM half in src/lib/claims/collect-dom.ts. Until then this entry is the record, and because the ledger is matched on the sentence verbatim, changing the expression makes it stale and fails.
figureProvenance.blocker: none - an accepted divergence, not a defect and not a backlog item

figureProvenanceNote: What this check reports are usually correctness bugs, not divergences: a provenance attribute rendering the name of a module nobody wrote is a provenance string, not provenance, so recording one here would file a defect as a measurement and let it sit. Four such bugs were found and fixed in src/ rather than listed. The one entry below is the other kind, and the reason it is accepted is written into it: a citation chosen by a database row cannot be a literal in the source, and the correctness the check was reaching for is now carried by the type instead. An entry belongs here only on those terms.
claimAttributeNote: Empty: exactly three components in this repository emit data-claim, data-claim-id or data-figure-kind — Claim, Figure and RelativeFigure — and all three carry data-provenance on the same element.
exemptNumeralNote: Empty: every element claiming the UI-chrome exemption names one of G1.11's six kinds as a literal, and none of them also carries a claim or figure marker.
reportBodyRegistrationNote: 746 prose blocks are rendered by the 162 report templates; 71 are registered canonical claims and 675 are not. src/lib/claims/presentation.ts returns a claim only when data/claims.json holds the key it looks up (report.<slug>.summary, report.<slug>.interpretation.rs<rsid>.<sorted genotype>, report.<slug>.study.<identifier>.<field>) and the canonical text_verbatim matches the template string character for character; anything else renders as bare prose with no numbered source link behind it. Closing an entry therefore means, per block: read the source, record it in data/citations.json with its access date and a supporting quotation of 25 words or fewer, and add the claim with text_verbatim identical to the template string and evidence whose accessed_on equals that source's access_date. That is a source review per statement, not a data-entry pass. The two batches that produced today's 71 statements each read the underlying publications and wrote up what they support — docs/sources/reviews and docs/sources/everyday/review.md — and between them covered eight reports out of 162.

The other nine reports have never been reviewed.
reportBodyRegistration.closing: Three interpretation claims for the FAAH report, whose sources are already in the register and are the cheapest registration in the catalogue; then nine reports of source review for the rest.

templateCitationRegistrationNote: The 162 templates carry 221 citation references; 20 resolve to an entry in data/citations.json and 201 do not. Across the whole catalogue those 201 references are 177 distinct sources, almost all PMIDs. A reference the register does not hold is a study the product names to a reader with no recorded access date, no supporting quotation and nothing in the repository showing the source was ever opened, which is exactly what C4 exists to prevent. Closing an entry means adding one data/citations.json record per distinct source: id, type, identifier, a URL an independent reader can resolve, the exact access date, a verbatim quotation of 25 words or fewer that supports what the report says, and the claim it supports. A PMID is a permanent identifier, so C4 needs no docs/sources snapshot for it; the quote and the access date still require the record to be opened and read. This group and the report-body group are the same work seen from two sides — the sources have to exist before the prose above them can be registered — so the two shrink together.

designatedSurfaceNote: G1.11 names seven surfaces whose string blocks must be emitted through the shared claim component with a mandatory citationId. Six of them diverge, in two ways the gate reports separately: a page whose module graph never reaches src/components/claims/claim.tsx cannot be emitting anything through it, and a surface no claim in data/claims.json is bound to has nothing registered to emit. Report bodies are the one designated surface that reaches the component and carries bound claims, which is why they appear in the two groups above rather than this one. All 71 claims name report routes, the account export contract and one mail fixture, so every other surface is unbound by construction.

designatedSurface.why: The five registered page routes that are this surface — legal.consents, legal.consent, legal.consent-version, legal.consent-diff and settings.consents — render their prose from the versioned artifacts in content/legal/** and from src/copy/upload/consent.ts, through the legal page components. No module on any of those five import graphs reaches src/components/claims/claim.tsx, so no consent summary sentence has a citation bound to it. Four of the five are also counted by the legal-pages entry below; the brief designates both surfaces and the overlap is real, not double counting.
designatedSurface.closing: Route the summary blocks through Claim, which needs each summary to be a canonical claim first. A consent summary's evidence is not a publication: it is the artifact itself and the statute or regulator text behind it, which data/citations.json admits as types statute, registry and regulator — each of which is a live web page and so needs a local snapshot under docs/sources/ as well.
designatedSurface.blocker: owner decision — whether a consent summary sentence is a claim in G1.11's sense, and what a statute or regulator citation looks like for one. Nothing in the tree answers it yet: data/citations.json holds no entry of type statute, registry or regulator at all.

designatedSurface.why: No claim in data/claims.json names any of the five consent routes. All 71 claims name /genome/[subject]/reports/<slug>, export:account-export-v1, and for eight of them the research-digest mail fixture, so this surface has nothing registered to render.
designatedSurface.closing: Follows the entry above: the binding exists once the summaries are registered claims. It is listed separately because the two are separately observable — a surface can reach the component and still have nothing bound to it, and vice versa.
designatedSurface.blocker: owner decision — the same one; a claim cannot be bound to a surface before it is decided that its prose is a claim.

designatedSurface.why: The corpus now exists and the surface is still unbound, which is a different finding from the one this entry used to hold. Built 2026-09-11: src/copy/glossary/index.ts is the readability corpus X7.1 designates, and it reads data/jargon.json rather than restating it, so a definition cannot drift between what a reader sees and what the readability gate scores. src/components/ui/glossary-term.tsx is line 884's GlossaryTerm - dotted underline, keyboard-focusable, expanding in place, never hover-only - and glossed-text.tsx glosses the first occurrence of a registered term in a copy string, which is line 829's 'on first use' and is also what keeps every gloss inside the first-viewport interactive budgets, since each one is a button. What is NOT done is the binding. Line 2570 designates glossary definitions as a surface where every string block must be emitted through the shared claim component with a mandatory citationId, and no claim in data/claims.json is bound to one. The definitions are real and already enforced for length by the readability gate; what is undecided is whether defining a word is a CLAIM that must cite a source.
designatedSurface.closing: Bind the definitions as claims once it is decided that they are claims, then wire GlossedText onto the surfaces where the 53 registered terms already appear in shipped copy. Until then the components exist and are tested but are deliberately not rendered to a reader, because doing so would put uncited prose on a surface the brief designates - the failure this check exists to catch, not a technicality to route around.
designatedSurface.blocker: owner decision - the same one the consent-summaries entry names: a claim cannot be bound to a surface before it is decided that its prose is a claim. Put to the operator on 2026-09-11, who chose to build the glossary and left the citation question open; this surface turns out to depend on it.

designatedSurface.why: All 22 registered legal page routes render prose written inline in the page modules under src/app/(marketing)/legal/** — src/app/(marketing)/legal/gina/page.tsx passes whole paragraphs of GINA explanation straight to LegalPage — or from the versioned artifacts in content/legal/**. None of the 22 import graphs reaches the shared claim component. These pages state what a statute protects and what it leaves out, which is precisely the class of external fact C4 requires a citation, an access date and a supporting quotation for.
designatedSurface.closing: Split each page's prose into what is Inherit's own policy, which needs no external citation, and what is a statement about law, which needs one of type statute or regulator with a snapshot under docs/sources/. Then render the second kind through Claim.
designatedSurface.blocker: owner decision — whether quoted statutory and regulator text should be a registered claim at all. The brief's other half of the answer is a verbatim region: X7.1 and line 1669 exclude text inside data-legal-verbatim from readability scoring entirely, and line 1855 allows controlled medical tokens inside one. No data-legal-verbatim region exists anywhere in src or content today, so the two mechanisms have never been reconciled. It matters concretely, because G1.11 caps a citation quote at 25 words and a quoted statutory passage will exceed that — a verbatim region and a registered claim cannot both be the answer for the same sentence.

designatedSurface.why: No claim in data/claims.json names any legal route, so there is nothing registered for these 22 pages to emit.
designatedSurface.closing: Follows the entry above and the decision it names.
designatedSurface.blocker: owner decision — the same verbatim-region question decides how much of these pages should ever be bound claims.

designatedSurface.why: The prompt the brief designates is the SYSTEM_PROMPT template literal in src/app/api/chat/route.ts, sent as the model's system message by src/lib/copilot/own-chat-route.ts. It states hard rules about what the model may assert — informational never diagnostic, association and probability shift with effect sizes — which are claims about how genetics works, phrased as instructions. The surface is not markup, so the only question the gate can ask is whether that prose is registered, and no claim is bound to it. It also cannot be bound as things stand: a claim surface locator is a page route path, export:<contract> or email:<file>, and a system prompt is none of the three, so there is no locator that names it.
designatedSurface.closing: Two decisions before any code: whether a system prompt's rules are claims in G1.11's sense, and, if so, what locator form names a prompt so data/claims.json can bind to one. Then the prompt prose moves somewhere registered — src/copy/copilot/ already holds the refusal strings that ship character for character — and each rule becomes a claim with its source.
designatedSurface.blocker: owner decision — is a system prompt's prose a claim, and what surface locator names it? Neither the brief nor docs/route-register.json gives one, and inventing a locator grammar to make a gate go green would be the wrong order of work.

designatedSurface.why: /embryos/compare renders from src/copy/embryos/compare.ts and the components under src/components/embryo/compare/, and neither reaches the shared claim component. The copy module already names its blocks with ids in the shape a claim_id takes — embryo.standing-statement, embryo.within-family.not-tested — and no claim of either name exists in data/claims.json, so the naming is a convention rather than a binding. The prose is claim-shaped in the strongest sense the product has: the standing statement asserts that no child has been born and followed up after embryos were compared this way, and the within-family sentences assert what has and has not been measured between siblings. docs/capability-register.md carries embryo comparison as not shipped and no ingest path creates a cohort, which is why the gap has not been felt by a reader yet.
designatedSurface.closing: Register the fixed sentences as canonical claims with their sources and render them through Claim. The mandated strings ship character for character already, so the text_verbatim match is the easy half; the evidence is the work.
designatedSurface.blocker: review — the standing statement is an assertion about the absence of outcome data, and citing an absence needs a source read and an owner willing to say which source establishes it.
review — the same source work; the binding is the last step of it, not a separate one.

designatedSurface.why: /family/portrait/[pairId] renders from src/copy/family/portrait.ts through the components under src/components/family/portrait/, none of which reaches the shared claim component. Two of its mandated strings are clinical statements about the world with no citation bound to them: the anti-D sentence, which tells a reader that an RhD-negative pregnant parent with an RhD-positive partner may need an injection and that this is routine care, and the sentence saying a blood test at any clinic can determine RhD where the file cannot. The trait cards are the honest counter-case and should not be read as part of this gap: every entry in the allowlist is unregistered today precisely because no accuracy figure can be cited, and each card says so and renders no figure and no claim block.
designatedSurface.closing: Register the clinical sentences as canonical claims against a registry or regulator source for routine anti-D prophylaxis, and render them through Claim. The trait cards need nothing until a genotype-to-phenotype table with a citable accuracy figure exists, at which point they need both.
designatedSurface.blocker: review — the anti-D sentence needs a human to choose and read a clinical guideline, record its access date and quote 25 words or fewer of it. It is the one place in this ledger where the missing citation is about immediate physical care.
